title: Companies (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Regulations, 2026

source.name: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan

verification.against: SECP PDF 'Companies (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Regulations, 2026' (S.R.O. 1976(I)/2026) downloaded from secp.gov.pk on 23 Nov 2026; editor declared regulator downloads verified (not a line-by-line check)

sections.title: Short title and commencement
text: (1) These regulations shall be called the Companies (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Regulations, 2026.
(2) These regulations shall come into force at once.

sections.title: Application
text: (1) These regulations shall apply to all companies including foreign companies.

(2) The provisions of these regulations shall have effect notwithstanding anything contained in the memorandum or articles of a company, or in any contract or agreement executed by it, or in any resolution passed by the company in general meeting or by its directors, whether the same be registered, executed or passed, as the case may be.

(3) For the purpose of these regulations, any existing scheme or business whether carried out through physical means or digital, online, electronic, social media, mobile applications, websites or any other technological platform and modern devices shall fall under these regulations if it exhibits the characteristics of an unlawful activity.

sections.title: Definitions
text: (1) In these regulations, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context, -
>(a) “Act” means the Companies Act, 2017 (XIX of 2017);
>(b) “multi-level marketing” or “MLM” means any scheme or business as referred to in regulation 5;
>(c) “participant” means any person who joins a sales or marketing structure with the expectation of receiving benefits or commissions;
>(d) “ponzi scheme” means a scheme or business as referred to in regulation 6;
>(e) “pyramid scheme” means any scheme or business activity as referred to in regulation 7;
>(f) “referral marketing” means an unlawful scheme or business as referred to in regulation 8; and
>(g) “unlawful activity” includes MLM, referral marketing, pyramid and ponzi schemes prohibited under these regulations.
(2) All other words and expressions used but not defined in these regulations shall have the same meanings as assigned thereto in the Act.

sections.title: Prohibition of unlawful activities
text: No company shall promote or carry out or assist in promoting or carrying out any unlawful activities.

sections.title: Multi-level marketing (MLM)
text: No company shall promote or carry on any one or more activities in its scheme or business, including but not limited to, where –
>(a) income or benefits are derived primarily from the recruitment of new members rather than genuine sale of goods to end consumers;
>(b) there is little or no evidence of bona fide product sales to ultimate users, or where products are merely incidental or absent altogether;
>(c) goods offered lacks reasonable market demand, serving merely as a disguise for recruitment-driven rewards;

>(d) high joining fees, subscriptions, or payments unrelated to the actual cost of products are required as a condition for participation with such funds being used to provide returns to earlier participants;

>(e) participants are compelled, directly or indirectly, to purchase large or unreasonable quantities of inventory in order to qualify for commissions, maintain rank, or secure continued participation;
>(f) exaggerated claims are made regarding income potential, financial returns, or the effectiveness and performance of products, creating unrealistic expectations for participants;
>(g) there is no clear, accessible, and equitable policy for the repurchase, refund, or return of unsold products; or
>(h) products sold are unregistered, unapproved, or constitute illegal imports or smuggled goods:
Provided that this shall not restrict bona fide direct selling activities where compensation is primarily derived from actual product sales to end consumers.

sections.title: Ponzi schemes
text: No company shall promote or carry on any one or more activities in its scheme or business, including but not limited to, that -
>(a) pays returns to earlier investors from funds contributed by new investors, rather than profits from commercial, trading, or business activity;
>(b) offers high, fixed, or guaranteed returns with little or no identifiable risk;
>(c) has no identifiable underlying business, asset, or revenue-generating activity; or
>(d) conceals, misrepresents or withholds information regarding the use or deployment of investor funds.

sections.title: Pyramid schemes
text: No company shall promote or carry on any one or more activities in its scheme or business, including but not limited to, that -
>(a) rewards participants primarily for enrolling or recruiting others rather than sales of genuine products;
>(b) lacks a clear written agreement or contractual terms governing participants’ rights and obligations;
>(c) requires excessive, or unreasonable product purchases as a condition for joining or continuing participation;
>(d) fails to provide fair, transparent or timely refund or buy-back policies for unsold products; or
>(e) allows or encourages multiple participation positions for the purpose of generating additional recruitment-based rewards.

sections.title: Referral marketing
text: No company shall carry on offers, promises, provide commissions, rewards, or benefits primarily for referring participants to that exhibit characteristic of MLM, pyramid or ponzi scheme.

sections.title: Penalty
text: Whoever including the company, directors and other officers fail or refuse to comply with or contravenes any requirement of these regulations shall be punishable as provided under sub-section (2) of section 512 of the Act, without prejudice to any action that may be taken under other provisions of the Act including winding up under section 301 thereof.
[No. SY/SECP/8/13]
